rationale: Round-3 codebase-pin review of 3018a659 (worktree clean, HEAD == reviewed commit). ASSIGNED DUTIES ALL VERIFIED. (1) The two new real-claim regressions RUN and PASS with real bd+git: TestNextCmd_ClaimGuard_SubdirectoryInvocationRefusesByteIdentical (51s — dirty entry-absent .gitignore in the spec worktree, claim invoked from a created subdirectory of it; refuses with the preserved 'cannot claim work' contract and proves total no-op on bd status, branch list, worktree list, and .gitignore bytes) and TestNextCmd_ClaimGuard_SymlinkAliasInvocationRefusesByteIdentical (57s — same dirt, claim invoked through a symlink alias of the worktree from a t.TempDir; refuses byte-identically and the alias's own target is verified unchanged). Both are exactly the two evasion shapes the pre-fix samePath(anchor, cwd) lexical gate got wrong. (2) TestContainedRel_SymlinkLeafKeepsOwnTrackedName RUNS and PASSES: a real git repo, a symlink leaf pointing at real-target.txt, and containedRel must report the symlink's OWN name — the leaf-resolving regression this round's own e2e fixture caught, now pinned at unit level; resolveContainingDirs's resolve-ancestors-only design in guard.go matches porcelain's report-symlinks-under-their-own-tracked-name behavior (which the round-2 symlinked refusal e2e variant exercises end-to-end, re-run green this round). (3) Diff confinement VERIFIED: exactly 7 files, all containment-mechanism-scoped — internal/next/guard.go (the samePath→toplevelOf/containedRel rework plus honest header-comment rewrite), internal/gitutil/gitops.go (Toplevel only, mirroring RevParseHEAD's shape), the two new test files, ADR-0025's amendment rewrite (now describes containment and the real-claim fixtures as the anti-drift pin, matching the shipped code — I read the full ADR diff), one new argv-audit entry for Toplevel (honest Count-1, operand shape identical to RevParseHEAD's: workdir via gitArgs + framework flags, no ref/id operand — matches the implementation), and a whitespace-only realignment of round-2's claimAnchorRoot allowlist entry (content byte-identical apart from column alignment). cmd/mindspec/next.go, internal/approve, and internal/harness are untouched this round. ADDITIONAL VERIFICATION BEYOND THE DUTIES: the full internal/next package passes uncached (all 33 containment+entangle unit tests, including the four toplevelOf legs — subdirectory and symlink-alias resolve to the same canonical identity, non-git dir degrades to cwd — and the outside-toplevel exclusion that prevents a '../'-leaking rel); internal/lint passes uncached so the ratchet counts are exact; go vet clean. Because the round-3 rework changed the enumeration's rel-base from cwd-relative to toplevel-relative, I also RE-RAN the round-2 legs that pin exactly that surface: EnumerationPin_RecordingEnabled (69s), EnumerationPin_GitignoreEntryAbsent (64s), and the symlinked refusal variant (46s — the one that stresses resolveContainingDirs hardest) — all PASS, no regression. The new third e2e leg, EnumerationPin_CustomWorktreeRootRecording (38s, PASS), correctly pins R3's SpecDir/claimAnchorRoot divergence shape: a decoy spec worktree at the custom root, the manifest seeded where SpecDir actually resolves it (repoRoot), a 2-path prediction asserted non-vacuously, and the claim invoked from repoRoot — the exact combination the pre-fix gate wrongly excluded. The containment design decision to trust recording's own resolution and gate purely on observed containment (rather than replicating SpecDir's probe) eliminates the duplicate-drift risk by construction.

findings.title: Cross-worktree entangleable rel-paths are inert by gitignore, not by construction
findings.detail: When `next` is invoked from the repo root while the spec worktree exists, containedRel(toplevel=repoRoot, anchor/.gitignore) yields ok=true with rel '.worktrees/worktree-spec-X/.gitignore' — the linked worktree is lexically inside the main tree's toplevel. That entry can normally never match porcelain output (the .worktrees/ dir is gitignored and is a separate working tree), so it is inert; and in the one state where it COULD interact — the repo root's own .gitignore missing the worktree-root entry, making '?? .worktrees/' collapsed untracked dirt whose ancestor rule then blocks — blocking is the conservative-correct outcome, since the claim's write really does land inside the reported dirt region. Recording the reasoning so a future reader doesn't mistake the cross-tree rel entry for a bug; no change required.

findings.title: Round-1 .beads/ pin-sensitivity note remains open (unchanged, still non-blocking)
findings.detail: Carried forward from rounds 1-2: the sandbox's blanket .beads/ gitignore keeps all enumeration-pin legs blind to a hypothetical future claim write on a tracked .beads path other than issues.jsonl. Nothing in round 3 changes this either way.
